title: Basic concepts of climate change
competency: Define climate change and distinguish weather, climate and global warming.

keywords.def: The condition of the atmosphere at a place on a particular day.
The conditions of the atmosphere in a certain place over many years.
The climate of one area, such as the Horn of Africa.
The average climate around the world.
The increase, over many years, of the average temperature of the Earth.
A change in the mean and/or variability of the climate that persists for decades or longer, from natural or human causes (IPCC).
Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change: set up by WMO and UNEP to assess climate change, its impacts and responses.
Gases such as CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O that trap heat and raise air temperature near the ground (GHGs).
CO₂: a greenhouse gas that strongly absorbs infrared radiation; it rises mainly from burning fossil fuels and deforestation.

en.text: Weather is the state of the atmosphere on a particular day; climate is the conditions of the atmosphere in a place over many years. The climate of one area, like the Horn of Africa, is a regional climate, and the average climate around the world is the global climate. The rise of the Earth's average temperature over many years is called global warming.

opts: No, one season is weather, not climate

items: Heavy rain in Addis Ababa this afternoon

The heat of the sun at noon

screens.text: Why must global warming be judged over decades, not from one weather event?
opts: Warming in any one year is small; it only becomes clear when averaged over many years
Thermometers work only once a decade
screens.ans: Warming in any one year is small; it only becomes clear when averaged over many years
screens.why: p.45: global warming in a given year is small and becomes significant only over decades.
screens.clue: Small yearly changes hide in the noise.

screens.text: Almost every summer for the past ten years has been hotter than usual. What is the best conclusion?
opts: It is likely a warming trend; longer records over decades would confirm it
It means nothing; only one year matters
It is weather and can never show climate change
It proves the whole world warmed equally
screens.ans: It is likely a warming trend; longer records over decades would confirm it
screens.why: A repeated pattern over years is a change in the mean: a climate signal. Decades of records make it certain.

ideas.name: The IPCC definition and climate connections

en.text: The IPCC defines climate change as a change in the state of the climate, seen in changes in the mean and/or variability of its properties, that persists for decades or longer, from natural variability or human activities. Because air, water and land are linked, warming spreads: greenhouse gases trap energy, the atmosphere and oceans warm, ice melts, sea level rises, storms strengthen and habitats change. Ice cores and direct observations show that CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O have increased over the last few centuries.

am.text: IPCC የአየር ንብረት ለውጥን ለአሥርተ ዓመታት የሚቆይ የአማካይ ወይም የመዋዠቅ ለውጥ ብሎ ይገልጻል፤ መንስኤው ተፈጥሮ ወይም ሰው ሊሆን ይችላል።

screens.title: Warmer air, then what?
screens.ask: The air above the oceans gets warmer. What happens next?
opts: The oceans absorb heat and warm, which can cause stronger storms
screens.after: Air, water and land are linked. A change in one place leads to changes somewhere else.

screens.title: Climate connections
paras: Greenhouse gases trap energy → warmer atmosphere.
Then: warmer oceans, more evaporation, melting snow and ice.
Warmer oceans → stronger storms and rising sea level.
More evaporation → more rain in some places; more droughts and wildfires in others.
Melting snow and ice → rising sea level; Earth absorbs more energy.
Plants and animals: shifting ranges, habitat loss, extinction.

screens.title: The IPCC definition
paras: Climate change is a change in the state of the climate.
It shows as changes in the mean and/or variability of its properties.
It lasts for an extended period: decades or longer.
The cause may be natural variability or human activities.
It is more than "it will get hotter".
Evidence: ice cores and direct observations show more CO₂, CH₄ and N₂O over the last few centuries.

screens.text: How is the IPCC definition different from narrower definitions of climate change?
opts: It includes change from both natural variability and human activities
It counts changes that last one year
screens.ans: It includes change from both natural variability and human activities
screens.why: p.36: "due to either natural variability or human activities". Some other definitions count only human-caused change.

screens.title: Match each box of Figure 2.2 with what it contains
pairs: Impacts on human and natural systems
screens.clue: Impacts are what happens to people and nature.

screens.text: In Figure 2.1, melting snow and ice lets Earth absorb more energy, which warms the atmosphere again. What does this loop do?
opts: It makes the warming speed itself up
screens.ans: It makes the warming speed itself up
screens.why: Less white ice reflects less sunlight; more energy is absorbed; the air warms and more ice melts.
screens.clue: Follow the arrow back to the centre.
